exposure: Infant characteristics (Apgar score, gestational age at birth, prenatal antibiotic exposure, vasopressor treatment, ventilator support)
Delivery characteristics (mode of delivery, rupture of membranes duration)
cohort: 142,410 term infants admitted to 326 neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) between 2011 and 2016 who were evaluated for EOS with blood, cerebrospinal fluid, or urine cultures
finding: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) was the most frequent cause of early-onset sepsis (EOS) in term infants admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of EOS.
